papers.title: Lifting Cocycles: From Heuristic to Theory
papers.abstract: The circular coordinates algorithm, a widely used tool in topological data analysis, relies on a lifting step to convert cocycles from a prime field to integer coefficients. We provide a rigorous analysis of this procedure, establishing a criterion for its success. We give an algebraic method for reducing the winding number under explicit torsion hypotheses. The torsion and coprimality hypotheses required by the winding number reduction are automatic in degree 1, because H^1(X; Z) is torsion-free. We extend these principles to homology, deriving analogous coefficientwise lifting criteria for cycles.

papers.title: Explicit covers and rigid obstructions for simplicial complexity: from spheres to surfaces
papers.abstract: The strict simplicial complexity $SC_{\rm strict}(K)$, Gonz\'alez's simplicial complexity at subdivision level zero, is one less than the least number of contiguity domains covering the ordered product $K\times K$. We bound it from both sides. For upper bounds, every product of two vertex stars is a domain, which gives $SC_{\rm strict}(K)\le\rho(K)-1$ for an exactly computable set-cover number $\rho(K)$; the bound is sharp on every even-dimensional simplex boundary. A GPU annealer that evolves whole systems of contiguity chains finds three-domain covers of $\partial\Delta^3,\dots,\partial\Delta^7$ and of the cube boundary. Seeded by star covers, it descends from $24$ to $5$ domains on the icosahedron boundary, and an exact SAT completion of its stalled state gives $SC_{\rm strict}\le3$ there. For lower bounds, a subcomplex of $K\times K$ is rigid if its two projections are joined by no contiguity chain of any length; $k$ domains can cover $K\times K$ only if $k$ classes of facets avoid every rigid subcomplex, a finite SAT problem. Rigid subcomplexes arise from hollow triangles over essential empty triangles and, on complexes without dominated vertices, from the graph of every order-preserving simplicial self-map other than the identity. The resultingchain-length-free bounds give $SC_{\rm strict}(\partial\Delta^{n+1})=2>1=TC(S^n)$ for $n=3,5,7,9$, $SC_{\rm strict}=2>1$ for the five-vertex M\"obius band, $SC_{\rm strict}\ge3>2$ for the seven-vertex torus, and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le5$ and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le6$ for two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$. They also sort the annealer's stalls: on these two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$, the Klein bottle and $\partial\Delta^4$, almost every uncovered facet closes a rigid subcomplex in every domain, while the icosahedron stall was a search failure.

papers.title: Integral permutation twisted cohomology: one auspicious twist is all you need
papers.abstract: We introduce a reduced form of permutation twisted cohomology for the derived category of permutation modules over any commutative ring. Unlike the twisted cohomology rings previously constructed by Balmer--Gallauer and Miller, this reduced twisted cohomology ring is only bigraded, twisted by a single, well-chosen endotrivial complex corresponding to the representation sphere arising from the (doubled) regular real representation of a group. We prove that over any commutative ring, the Balmer spectrum of the derived category of permutation modules is homeomorphic to the projectivization of the spectrum of the reduced twisted cohomology ring. Moreover, we show that if the base ring is Noetherian, this ring is finite over the finitely generated subalgebra generated by the forerunners, certain $p$-local isomorphisms, of the twist. We apply these results to further analyze the geometry of permutation modules, determine the local Picard group of the geometric open of the Balmer spectrum, and resolve other questions posed by Miller. We include an appendix giving a general criterion for finite generation of twisted cohomology rings in tensor-triangular geometry.

papers.title: The generalized Segal conjecture and the coalgebraic Frobenius
papers.abstract: We prove the generalized Segal conjecture, extending work of Bergsaker and Rognes and confirming a conjecture by the author: for every finite group $G$ and every bounded-below spectrum $X$, the Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel norm $N_e^G X$ becomes Borel-complete after completion at the augmentation ideal of the Burnside ring. Equivalently, for every non-trivial finite $p$-group $G$, the proper Tate diagonal $X\to(X^{\otimes G})^{\varphi G}$ is a $p$-completion. The proof reduces to the case $X=\Fp$, established by Bergsaker and Rognes, and removes the finiteness hypotheses from their theorem by abstract manipulations. As an application of this result, we refine the coalgebraic Frobenius to an oriented circle action (i.e. an action of the monoidal category $B\mathbb N$) on the category of bounded-below, $p$-complete $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-coalgebras, confirming another conjecture by the author. The construction is based on Yuan's approach to Frobenius actions via partial algebraic $K$-theory.

papers.title: Deleted square of a cone over a graph
papers.abstract: The deleted square of a topological space is a subspace of the Cartesian product of this space with itself, obtained by removing the diagonal. Conjecturally, the deleted square of a cone over a graph has the homotopy type of a wedge sum of spheres of dimensions at most 3. We propose a geometric construction that is a key motivation for the conjecture and provides a major step towards its proof, while yielding direct results on deleted squares of certain families of graphs.

papers.title: Graded Monoidal Categories and Internalization
papers.abstract: In stable homotopy theory, there are a variety of ways to construct a point-set level smash product of spectra, each with its own advantages and limitations. These constructions often involve internalizing some graded external product. In this paper, we aim to formalize this process through a general categorical framework, providing a common language for these constructions. We propose a general theory for internalizing a graded monoidal product, investigate its 2-categorical properties, and use this framework to recover both Day convolution and the smash product of $S$-modules.

papers.title: The pentagonal tensor and the fourth obstruction to formality
papers.abstract: Let \(A\) be a connected graded commutative differential graded algebra over \(\mathbb Q\) whose cohomology is a finite-dimensional Poincar\'e duality algebra of formal dimension \(N\ge2\). Assuming that its Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes, we prove that the normalized pentagonal tensor of Nagy and Nordstr\"om, in [preprint (2021), arXiv:2105.13660], vanishes if and only if the fourth Harrison obstruction vanishes after eliminating the third operation. This gives a fourth-order counterpart to the third-order comparison of Fiorenza and L\^e, in [Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5), published online 7 March 2025], and answers the vanishing question in L\^e's proposed comparison, in [preprint (2026), arXiv:2603.01219], under the hypothesis that the Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes. The result applies to closed, connected, oriented manifolds with no upper dimension bound. We also extend Zhou's sphere-bundle formality criterion in [Algebr. Geom. Topol. 25 (2025), pp. 2297--2315] to two-stage oriented sphere bundles with positive odd fibre dimensions over a closed, connected, oriented, rationally formal base, provided that the second Euler class is pulled back from the original base. Their total spaces are rationally formal precisely when the Bianchi-Massey and normalized pentagonal tensors vanish. Our method develops the model-based strategy in Zhou's proof within a commutative bar-cobar framework, providing a starting point for constructing higher tensors and comparing them with higher-order formality obstructions.

papers.title: $E_d$-Enhancements of $L_\infty$-Algebras Associated to Secondary Polytopes
papers.abstract: We study $E_d$-enhancements of the geometric $L_\infty$-algebras associated to secondary polytopes of finite configurations in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$. We construct an action of the semialgebraic chains of the Fulton--MacPherson operad on the shifted algebra $B_A=\mathfrak g_A[1-d]$ when $|A|\leq3d$. The action recovers the prescribed higher Lie operations on fundamental chains. The construction is obtained from a general extension theorem for weighted shifted $L_\infty$-algebras, using reflection to control relative cohomology obstructions. For $|A|\leq3d-1$, the resulting reflection-compatible integration actions are homotopic relative to their shifted Lie structure. We also give an abstract enhancement without a cardinality bound, direct formulas for circuits, and explicit operations for convex pentagons and hexagons.

papers.title: Splitting of abelian varieties in motivic stable homotopy category
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss the motivic stable homotopy type of abelian varieties. For an abelian variety over a perfect field $k$, a top-dimensional cell always splits off in the motivic stable homotopy category $\text{SH}(k)$. Let $k=\mathbb{R}$. If $X$ is a real abelian variety of positive dimension $g$, there is, for $\mathbb{Z}[1/(2g)!]\subset\Lambda\subset\mathbb{Q}$, a concrete splitting in $\text{SH}(\mathbb{R})_\Lambda$ determined by the Deninger--Murre decomposition of the motive of $X$ and the real points $X(\mathbb{R})$. With rational coefficients, we also discuss its refinement from the viewpoint of K\"unnemann's Lefschetz decomposition.

papers.title: On the splitting of surfaces in motivic stable homotopy category
papers.abstract: Over a perfect field of characteristic zero, we study when the top cell splits off from a pointed smooth projective surface in motivic stable homotopy, with K3 surfaces as the main example. Adams--Riemann--Roch and the motivic Adams relations give a uniform top-codimension annihilator. This yields an integral extreme-cell splitting in particular for complex projective K3 surfaces. Chow--Witt correspondences also yield noncanonical three-term decompositions of Milnor--Witt motives with extreme Tate summands and a nilpotence criterion for lifting finite systems of Chow projectors. In positive characteristic, the annihilator statement holds after inverting the characteristic.

papers.title: Marked Persistent Homology: Circuits and Bordisms
papers.abstract: The barcode of a persistence module does not determine the relations among prescribed cycles. We encode these relations by a filtration of kernels in fixed coordinates, whose circuits can ramify into overlapping families and later recombine, unlike the merge-tree structure of degree-zero persistence. The kernels recover the marked image module and admit simultaneous rational bordism realizations. An explicit planar Vietoris-Rips filtration exhibits the circuit changes and their surface fillings.

papers.title: A $p$-adic de Rham complex
papers.abstract: This is the second in a sequence of three articles exploring the relationship between commutative algebras and $E_\infty$-algebras in characteristic $p$ and mixed characteristic. Given a topological space $X,$ we construct, in a manner analogous to Sullivan's $A_{PL}$-functor, a strictly commutative algebra over $\padic$ which we call the de Rham forms on $X$. We show this complex computes the singular cohomology ring of $X$. We prove that it is quasi-isomorphic as an $E_\infty$-algebra to the Berthelot-Ogus-Deligne \emph{d\'ecalage} of the singular cochains complex with respect to the $p$-adic filtration. We show that one can extract concrete invariants from our model, including Massey products which live in the torsion part of the cohomology. We show that if $X$ is formal then, except at possibly finitely many primes, the $p$-adic de Rham forms on $X$ are also formal. We conclude by showing that the $p$-adic de Rham forms provide, in a certain sense, the "best functorial strictly commutative approximation" to the singular cochains complex.

papers.title: Proper kernels in microlocal sheaf theory
papers.abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be real analytic manifolds and let $\Lambda \subseteq T^*X$ and $\Sigma \subseteq T^*Y$ be closed conic subanalytic singular isotropics. Given a sheaf $K \in \mathrm{Sh}_{-\Lambda \times \Sigma}(X \times Y)$ microsupported in $-\Lambda \times \Sigma$, consider the convolution functor $(-) \ast K \colon \mathrm{Sh}_{\Lambda}(X) \rightarrow \mathrm{Sh}_{\Sigma}(Y)$ from sheaves microsupported in $\Lambda$ to sheaves microsupported in $\Sigma$. We show that the convolution functor $(-) \ast K$ preserves compact objects if and only if for each $x \in X$, the restriction $K|_{\{x\} \times Y} \in \mathrm{Sh}_\Sigma(Y)$ is a compact object. By a result of Kuo-Li, the functor sending a sheaf kernel $K$ to the convolution functor $(-) \ast K$ is an equivalence between the category $\mathrm{Sh}_{-\Lambda \times \Sigma}(X \times Y)$ of sheaves microsupported in $-\Lambda \times \Sigma$ and the category of cocontinuous functors from $\mathrm{Sh}_\Lambda(X)$ to $\mathrm{Sh}_\Sigma(Y)$. We therefore classify all cocontinuous functors that preserve compact objects between the two categories. Our approach is entirely categorical and requires minimal input from geometry: we introduce the notion of a proper object in a compactly generated stable infinity-category and study its properties under strongly continuous localizations to obtain the result. The main geometric input is the analysis of compact and proper objects of the category of $P$-constructible sheaves for a triangulation $P$ of a manifold $Z$ via the exit path category $\mathrm{Exit}(Z, P) \simeq P$. Along the way, we show that a sheaf $F \in \mathrm{Sh}_\Lambda(X)$ is proper if and only if it has perfect stalks, which is equivalent to a result of Nadler.

papers.title: On the homotopy types of $4$-dimensional toric orbifolds
papers.abstract: The cohomological rigidity problem for toric orbifolds asks when an integral cohomology isomorphism implies a homotopy equivalence. In this paper we reformulate the cohomological rigidity problem in the context of $4$-dimensional toric orbifolds by introducing what we call proper isomorphisms, a variant of a concept studied by J.H.C. Whitehead. We prove that each proper isomorphism class of $4$-dimensional toric orbifolds contains at most two distinct homotopy types, and that the two classifications agree in certain special circumstances.

papers.title: Sectional category versus module sectional category for retractive maps
papers.abstract: We construct a map between simply connected rational spaces of finite rational type which admits a homotopy retraction and satisfies $msecat(p)=2<secat(p)=3$. The target is the rationalization of a simply connected twelve-dimensional CW complex with eleven cells, and is rationally hyperbolic. This disproves Carrasquel--Vera's conjecture for retractive maps.

papers.title: On bordism classes of symmetric products of surfaces
papers.abstract: We explicitly determine the complex bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a complex curve of genus $g$. In particular, we provide an explicit formula expressing this class as an integral linear combination of bordism classes of products of complex projective spaces. Similarly, we determine the unoriented bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a non-orientable surface of genus $g$ (i.e., $\#_{i=1}^{g+1}\mathbb R P^2$). It turns out that these classes are also expressed as a $\mathbb Z_2$-linear combination of bordism classes of products of even-dimensional real projective spaces. We also give an affirmative answer to a non-orientable version of the Blagojevi\'c--Gruji\'c--\v{Z}ivaljevi\'c conjecture stating that the topological type of any symmetric product of a noncompact surface of finite type determines the topological type of the surface itself.
